subject: TTFT handshake, backpressure & SSE pacing — next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@quantia.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantia.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: TTFT handshake, backpressure & SSE pacing — next steps

Hi Alex / Samir —

Thanks for the demo and the candid discussion this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on TTFT and streaming behavior for the pilot. I tried to keep this tight so engineering can action items.

Summary of the ask from your side:
- Target Time-to-First-Token (TTFT): 120ms median, 250ms p95 for 512-token prompts under steady-state traffic.
- Streaming mode: prefer SSE to start (simplicity on client) but need robust reconnection/handshake behavior for mobile clients.
- Chunk cadence: small, frequent chunks (8–16 tokens/chunk) to improve perceived latency; tolerant to a few extra round trips for cold starts.
- Concurrency expectation: 400 concurrent active users with average request rate of 0.2 r/s each (burst tolerance to 1.2 r/s/user for short windows).

Proposed Redwood items to validate: 
1) We'll run a 72-hour TTFT probe (pilot) from our dedicated pool to measure median/p95 at your sample traffic mix. See attached draft probe plan. [Attachment: ttft-probe-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
2) We'll provide an SSE handshake guide and a small client snippet that includes reconnect/backoff behavior. Also attaching the protocol diagram. [Attachment: sse-protocol-diagram.png]
3) Engineering will validate whether 8–16 token chunking with our default batching preserves your p95 target; if not, we will test 24-token cadence as an alternative.

Immediate asks for Quantia: 
- Confirm whether mobile sessions must use long polling as a fallback or if SSE reconnect is acceptable.
- Send a 30-second representative sample of your prompt distribution (short/medium/long) so we can calibrate cache/warm-start behavior.

Next internal sync: Ben / Karthik & I — can you confirm availability for a technical dry run tomorrow afternoon PST (14 Dec 15:00–16:00 PST)?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate next steps once I hear back on the two quick items above.

—
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0191

On Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:50:11 -0800 Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@quantia.ai> wrote:
> Great session — appreciate the clear breakdown. I’ve looped in Samir (mobile lead) because of the SSE question.
>
> Quick clarifications:
> - The 120ms median is our ideal; we understand p95 will be higher. If you can hit 200–220ms p95 that’d be workable.
> - For mobile, SSE reconnect is OK as long as client-side jitter/backoff is documented. We don’t expect long polling except for older OS versions.
>
> Attaching our initial traffic matrix in the follow-up.
>
> Alex
> 
From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@quantia.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantia.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 14:40:22 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT handshake, backpressure & SSE pacing — next steps

Thanks Rachel — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

1) We can provide a 3-minute sampled prompt distribution CSV by EOD. Will include token-length buckets and common system prompts.
2) For p95 we’re stretching to 220ms as Alex mentioned. If Redwood can show a plan for keeping cold-starts under control (priming/KV cache strategy) we can accept a slightly higher p95 during the first 10 minutes of a volume spike.
3) We also want to confirm how Redwood handles backpressure when client network is slow — do you buffer until a chunk is ready, or stream partial token sequences? That behavior impacts perceived latency on flaky mobile networks.

If you can outline the backpressure behavior and recommended client reconnect values, we can lock down the pilot acceptance criteria.

— Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@quantia.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantia.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 16:10:05 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT handshake, backpressure & SSE pacing — next steps

Alex / Rachel / Samir —

Quick engineering note from my side after a short review with Karthik: 
- On backpressure: Redwood will emit tokens as they are produced; for slow client networks we can optionally batch up to X tokens (configurable) before flush. Default behavior is immediate emit to preserve perceived latency; if Quantia prefers smoother payloads we can set a 12-token flush threshold.
- For startup priming: we recommend a 1-token priming prefix on warm-starts (cheap) and a 10s warm-window where we keep a hot KV cache for that session. That should help the p95 on short bursts.
- SSE reconnect guidance: suggest exponential backoff starting at 250ms, max backoff 30s with jitter. We’ll include a client snippet.

I’ll spin up a short internal test that simulates your burst pattern (0.2 r/s typical, 1.2 r/s bursts) — aiming to run by tomorrow morning PST and share results mid-day.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
